Interface VirtualServer

All Known Subinterfaces:
VirtualServerRmi, VirtualServerSocket
All Known Implementing Classes:
RmiClient, RmiServer, SocketServerHandler
public interface VirtualServer
Technology-agnostic interface representing the server, as seen from the client side.

This interface decouples the client's command-sending logic from the underlying transport: both the Socket and RMI implementations expose the same three game actions, so the rest of the client code (e.g. view.tui.CLIView) can issue commands without knowing whether they travel over a socket stream or an RMI remote call.

Concrete implementations:

  • RMI: RmiClient
  • Socket: SocketServerHandler

  • Method Details

    • joinGame

      void joinGame(int numPlayers, String nickname) throws Exception
      Sends a request to join or create a game with the given number of players.
      Parameters:
      numPlayers - the desired game size
      nickname - the player's chosen display name
      Throws:
      Exception - if the request cannot be sent (transport failure) or is rejected by the server (game-rule violation)

    • placeTotem

      void placeTotem(String nickname, char position) throws Exception
      Sends a request to place the player's totem on the given offer-track slot.
      Parameters:
      nickname - the nickname of the player performing the action
      position - the offer-track slot (A–G) on which the totem should be placed
      Throws:
      Exception - if the request cannot be sent or is rejected by the server

    • takeCard

      void takeCard(String nickname, String cardId) throws Exception
      Sends a request to take a card from the showed rows.
      Parameters:
      nickname - the nickname of the player performing the action
      cardId - the identifier of the card to take

      Exception - if the request cannot be sent or is rejected by the server

    • disconnect

      default void disconnect() throws Exception
      Notifies the server that the client is disconnecting cleanly.

      Default no-op implementation: not all transports require an explicit disconnect notification (e.g. closing a socket stream is itself the signal), so implementations override this only when a transport-specific cleanup call is needed.

      Throws:
      Exception - if the disconnect notification cannot be sent
